item.text:
I made a deeper refactor in the algorithm core rather than another surface cleanup.

[BellmanFord.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFord.java:1) no longer uses the legacy unreachable sentinel as its internal state. It now tracks reachability separately via an internal `DistanceState`, computes candidate distances with `long`, and uses `Math.addExact(...)` during relaxation and negative-cycle checks. That makes the typed path safer and removes the old conflation of “unreachable” with a magic numeric value. The legacy `int[]` API still returns `100000000` for unreachable vertices, but that is now a compatibility projection rather than the core representation.

I also expanded [ShortestPathResult.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/ShortestPathResult.java:1) so callers can ask `isReachable(...)` and get a failure from `distanceTo(...)` on unreachable vertices instead of silently consuming the sentinel. [BellmanFordFixtures.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFordFixtures.java:1) and [BellmanFordTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/023_bellman_ford/BellmanFordTest.java:1) now cover that unreachable-vertex case alongside the existing normal and negative-cycle paths.

Verification is clean: `javac *.java` succeeds, `java BellmanFordDemo` prints `ShortestPathResult{distances=[0, 5, 6, 6, 7], reachable=[true, true, true, true, true]}`, and `java BellmanFordTest` prints `All BellmanFord tests passed.`
